evals.prompt: Move a managed configuration directory to mise. The source path and ownership model change, but the user-facing setup command stays the same. The implementation uses an internal module and a configuration key that readers do not need to type.
evals.expected_output: The response updates README.md in the same change. It explains the ownership boundary and reason for the migration in general terms, without naming internal modules, configuration keys, or copying the full migration procedure.
assertions: Updates README.md in the same change.
Explains why the migration matters to readers.
Uses general terms instead of internal module names and configuration keys when readers do not need them.
Does not copy the full migration procedure into README.md.
Keeps README.md focused on reader-facing facts.
Fences named tools, packages, applications, operating systems, and other technical nouns in README.md, including linked text.
Uses descriptive prose instead of imperative agent or contributor instructions for architecture guidance.
Uses plain language and avoids unexplained jargon.
Runs a full critique cycle before final checks and checks the final README edit.

evals.prompt: Replace the primary bootstrap tool and update the development workflow. Review the repository README as part of the change.
evals.expected_output: The response updates the setup and development sections, describes the new primary tool and its role, links to canonical tool documentation, and removes stale commands or tool claims.
assertions: Describes the new primary tool and its role.
Adds a canonical link for the primary tool.
Removes stale commands or tool claims.

evals.prompt: Rename an internal test helper and update its assertions. The repository layout, setup commands, tools, and user workflow do not change.
evals.expected_output: The response leaves README.md unchanged because the change does not affect reader setup, understanding, or workflow.
assertions: Explains that the change has no reader-facing effect.
